text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Colonel John Dungs, military administrator of midwestern Delta state, imposes a dusk-to-dawn curfew on troubled oil town of Warri. The town, a part of Delta state, has seen violent protests for most of the week over relocation of a local government headquarters.

- Salim Ahmed Salim, secretary general of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), is among dignitaries who have arrived in northern Kaduna city for Saturday's opening of the 7th OAU African trade and tourism fair.
- Nigeria's Lagos-based lawyers' groups criticises the military government's plan to introduce a press court, saying it is aimed at curtailing journalists' freedom.
- Security tightened at Nigerian borders to ensure robbers do not escape across them after raids, assistant inspector general of police Hamisu Ali-Jos says.
